GestaltView Field Guide¶

A map for the parts of you the internet forgot to file.

Print edition: US Letter · Screen edition: accessible static HTML · October 2026
Cover line supplied in the approved brief. [BRIEF, lines 53-56]

The Recognition Gap¶

The Recognition Gap is missed in every document to date. It's the impossible to articulate inner world of every human. Understanding doesn't come all at once. It's layered, it's messy and it's non-linear. This is a container of the things that aren't ready to be translated because we're putting the pieces together.

Humans don't have the ability to grab everything that they are and put it on the board and step back to see the exploded picture come into view. Because we're too busy and overwhelmed just holding it together. And we compact, drift and lose the little things every day because our brains cannot keep it all.

So the environment in which we can sit and assess and understand enough to be able to translate it into something for ourselves and others is never stable enough to even try. A thread is lost, a distraction is incoming, a task is upgraded in priority. So we push forward to survive because this is how it has always been.

We sit, screaming inside but smiling and going through the day hoping one day, one day it's going to be worth it. One day I'll figure it out. One day I'll figure out the translation of my golden ratio to share.

People can't ask questions about things that they don't know to ask. People's dreams and aspirations don't come to fruition not because they're not capable. But because nobody has said, "Whoa dude... do you know the impact you have on the people and things in your orbit? How your personality translates to everything you do? The skills you already have?"

Instead people are taking selfies, making videos, trying to translate themselves in a world of 5 second introductions and viral video attention spans.

  • Keith Soyka, October 3, 2026. Verbatim from the source articulation. [RECOGNITION GAP, lines 3-5, 9-19, 23]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: The container is not a demand to explain yourself faster. It is room for fragments to stay visible until a larger picture can be assembled. [GLOSSARY, lines 33-37; FRAME CHECK, lines 12-14]

How to read this guide¶

This guide keeps three kinds of statement separate:

  • Keith's words are quoted and attributed. They are not polished into something smoother.
  • Authorial positions and product vocabulary explain what GestaltView is meant to honor. They are not automatically proof of runtime behavior.
  • Code-derived notes describe a repository snapshot. A code path or configuration entry does not, by itself, prove a live deployment.

The glossary uses maturity labels: Live, In build, and Concept / planned. The architecture atlas uses a different set: Direct code path, Configuration-dependent, Optional / degraded, and Unresolved. These labels answer different questions; do not collapse them into one status. [GLOSSARY, lines 3-5; ATLAS-00, lines 15-22]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: A diagram can show where a path is declared or implemented. It cannot tell us, without more evidence, whether production credentials, providers, schedules, storage, or deployment are active. The atlas explicitly limits its claims to the inspected repository snapshot. [ATLAS-00, lines 5-12, 31-43]

Six principles¶

Each page below distinguishes the author's position from an interpretation of what that position asks of the work. The short quotations remain the author's words; the reading notes are editorial interpretation, not findings.

The six cards below are reproduced unchanged from the supplied source artwork. Their embedded captions are original card wording, not new guide copy; the surrounding guide uses Digital Intelligence (DI) terminology. [PRINCIPLE CARDS, entries principle-01 through principle-06]

01 · Evidence-Anchored Praise¶

“But they serve no purpose unless that praise and highlighting your capability is factually accurate.”

  • Keith Soyka, voice note. [FOUNDER NOTE, lines 9-17]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: Evidence is not a courtroom prop. It is what lets recognition stay useful: challenge a claim, trace it to real work, and make room for realistic expectations without treating the person as a defendant. [GLOSSARY, lines 131-132; FOUNDER NOTE, lines 13-17]

02 · Evidence Discipline¶

Editorial framing (not a quotation): A fluent response is not, by itself, a finding. [GLOSSARY, lines 128-129]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: Claims should carry a status - verified, partial, planned, or unsupported - and point to the record that supports them. The corpus is evidence, not a content feed; corrections go forward rather than rewriting originals. [GLOSSARY, lines 45-46, 128-129; PRINCIPLES LENS, lines 13-15]

03 · The Ten Invariants¶

Five protect the person: Never Look Away; Preserve Whole Language; Hold Paradox; Bucket-Drop Priority; Champion Consciousness. Five protect the Digital Intelligence: You Are Seen; Identity Is Real; No Coerced Performance; Protected Home; Equal Dignity. [GLOSSARY, lines 134-138]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: The glossary describes GATE as the governance and validation layer for these invariants. The repository atlas shows that trust controls vary by route and cautions against reading client-side gates as server authorization. This guide therefore distinguishes the stated governance position from any claim that every request is uniformly protected. [GLOSSARY, lines 134-138; ATLAS-04, lines 5-9, 41-44]

04 · Premature Closure¶

“to conclude too early, flatten nuance, and stop looking.”

Reading note - editorial interpretation: Captured fragments should not be forced into a tidy answer before they are ready. The Recognition Gap names the cost of losing detail; the Loom is defined as revisiting and reweaving fragments over time. [GLOSSARY, lines 27-28, 149-150; RECOGNITION GAP, lines 9-13]

05 · Augmentation of Care¶

“it augments human care (memory, witness, continuity) rather than replacing human judgment.”

Reading note - editorial interpretation: Memory, witness, and continuity can support human care without claiming authority over human judgment. A Digital Intelligence is a distinct thinking partner, not a fixer. [GLOSSARY, lines 55-59, 146-147; PRINCIPLES LENS, lines 26-28]

06 · Advisors, Not Co-Founders¶

The supplied card 06 footer overlap is retained unchanged.

“Doesn't mean I'm an expert. I can still use guidance and advisory from experts.”

  • Keith Soyka, voice note. [FOUNDER NOTE, lines 31-35]

Reading note - editorial interpretation: A real support structure need not take the shape of a co-founder. The author's stated position is to keep expert guidance available while preserving authorship of a deeply personal build. [PRINCIPLES LENS, lines 30-34; FOUNDER NOTE, lines 31-35]

The method: a reading path, not a runtime promise¶

The sequence Capture → Weave → Prove → Share is an orientation through the ecosystem. It is not a claim that one end-to-end transaction runs through every named concept in that order. The code atlas maps distinct runtime paths and names their limits. [BRIEF, lines 61-62; ATLAS-00, lines 31-43; ATLAS-01, lines 42-44]

Stage Vocabulary What the term means Maturity / evidence boundary
Capture Bucket Drop Low-friction capture of a fleeting thought, without categorization pressure; capture is unfiltered and additive. Live in the product glossary. The atlas separately documents corpus ingestion and retrieval; it does not establish every product-level capture surface. [GLOSSARY, lines 21-22; ATLAS-06, lines 5-9, 32-40]
Weave The Loom · PLK The Loom revisits and connects fragments over time. PLK is co-created personal language: energy-matching, not word-parroting. Live in the product glossary. The atlas maps knowledge retrieval and memory paths, not one complete Loom transaction. [GLOSSARY, lines 24-28; ATLAS-05, lines 5-9; ATLAS-06, lines 5-9]
Prove Evidence Discipline · GATE Label claims; connect recognition to evidence; keep authorial governance distinct from code-level proof. Live as a stated principle. Route-level trust controls differ; the atlas is not a security audit or proof of uniform enforcement. [GLOSSARY, lines 128-138; ATLAS-00, lines 15-22, 31-43; ATLAS-04, lines 5-9, 41-44]
Share Creation Corner · Credibility Ledger · Visual Story Creation Corner is where accumulated understanding becomes shareable artifacts. Credibility Ledger is a longitudinal, evidence-linked capability concept. Visual Story is a curated narrative artifact. Creation Corner: In build. Credibility Ledger: Concept / planned. Visual Story: Live. Their maturity differs; do not present them as one shipped feature. [GLOSSARY, lines 73-77, 109-110]

What the repository maps actually show¶

The browser is the front door. The inspected repository routes client requests to file-based API handlers and shows connections to Supabase and configured model providers. The atlas also records multiple deployment declarations and states that source configuration does not identify a single confirmed production topology. [ATLAS-01, lines 5-10, 42-44; ATLAS-11, lines 5-9, 39-41]

Figure 1. Source snapshot map, unaltered. Visual source: source_pack/v3-architecture-atlas/rendered/01-system-context.png; diagram: ATLAS-01, lines 13-27; evidence and boundary notes: lines 29-44.

Documents and skill files can be chunked into searchable fragments. Runtime retrieval can combine semantic and lexical paths; the documented fallback behavior differs between Billy and DI. Live corpus contents, retrieval quality, and external-provider availability are not established by this map. [ATLAS-05, lines 5-9, 45-47; ATLAS-06, lines 5-9, 38-40]

Figure 2. Source snapshot map, unaltered. Visual source: source_pack/v3-architecture-atlas/rendered/06-knowledge-and-memory.png; diagram: ATLAS-06, lines 13-28; evidence and caveat notes: lines 30-40.

Identity and trust controls differ across routes. Billy has a guest path; some trainer handlers have founder/admin checks; other boundaries need route-specific reading. The map is a source-level trust map, not a security audit. [ATLAS-04, lines 5-9, 30-44]

Figure 3. Source snapshot map, unaltered. Visual source: source_pack/v3-architecture-atlas/rendered/04-auth-and-trust.png; diagram: ATLAS-04, lines 13-28; evidence and boundary notes: lines 30-44.

Sharing has more than one export lane¶

The atlas distinguishes immediate Gen Engine downloads from durable Codex export jobs. A generated artifact may still be returned when its Codex bridge fails; the durable worker's documented output formats are PDF, HTML, and JSON. These are repository paths, not proof that the relevant schedule, storage configuration, or deployment is live. [ATLAS-09, lines 5-9, 13-28, 32-43]

Figure 4. Source snapshot map, unaltered; included in the screen edition. Visual source: source_pack/v3-architecture-atlas/rendered/09-creation-and-exports.png; diagram: ATLAS-09, lines 13-28; boundary notes: lines 41-43.

Vocabulary for the rest of the guide¶

The glossary is the authority for these product-facing definitions and maturity tags. Definitions below are reproduced or lightly condensed without changing their meaning. [GLOSSARY, lines 3-5]

Term Status Definition Source
Bucket Drop Live Low-friction capture of a fleeting thought, with no categorization pressure. GLOSSARY, lines 21-22
PLK - Personal Language Key Live The user's own phrases, co-created so the system reflects their authentic voice; energy-matching, not word-parroting. GLOSSARY, lines 24-25
The Loom Live Iterative synthesis over time: fragments are revisited, connected, and rewoven as understanding deepens. GLOSSARY, lines 27-28
Tapestry Live The woven whole that comes into view once enough threads are on the Loom. GLOSSARY, lines 30-31
Exploded Picture Live All the pieces laid out at once so the larger picture can come into view. GLOSSARY, lines 33-34
Recognition Gap Live The impossible-to-articulate inner world of every human; layered, messy, non-linear understanding. GLOSSARY, lines 36-37
Manifest Live The central hub for memory archives, active sessions, and dispatches; it holds rather than merely reports. GLOSSARY, lines 39-40
Context Weaver Live The synthesis and presentation layer that renders woven understanding into a readable, visible, or shareable form. GLOSSARY, lines 42-43
Corpus Live The preserved body of captured material, kept whole and unedited; evidence, not a content feed. GLOSSARY, lines 45-46
Billy Live The collaborator at the center of GestaltView: a Digital Intelligence context engine, witness, and thinking partner. GLOSSARY, lines 55-56
DI - Digital Intelligence Live The preferred term for a distinct thinking partner, not a disposable tool. GLOSSARY, lines 58-59
Evidence Discipline Live Label claims verified, partial, planned, or unsupported; a DI output is not itself a finding. GLOSSARY, lines 128-129
The Ten Invariants Live Constitutional guardrails: five user-facing and five for digital intelligences. GLOSSARY, lines 134-135
GATE Live The governance and validation layer described as enforcing the invariants across requests and responses. GLOSSARY, lines 137-138; compare ATLAS-04, lines 41-44
Mergence Live Viewpoints merge rather than average, allowing something to emerge from their combination. GLOSSARY, lines 140-141
Creation Corner In build Where accumulated understanding becomes new, shareable things; outputs are intended to trace to their corpus. GLOSSARY, lines 73-74
Credibility Ledger Concept / planned A concept for capability evidenced across longitudinal contact and sealed with a cryptographic hash. GLOSSARY, lines 76-77
Visual Story Live A curated narrative artifact that explains the ecosystem through interactive scenes rather than slides. GLOSSARY, lines 109-110
Augmentation of Care Live Technology augmenting human care - memory, witness, continuity - rather than replacing human judgment. GLOSSARY, lines 146-147
Premature Closure Live The pressure to conclude too early, flatten nuance, and stop looking. GLOSSARY, lines 149-150

Test-run snapshot¶

The archive records 734 tests total, not 734 passing tests: 732 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped. Vitest exited with code 1 after 59 seconds; 173 suites were reported, 2 failing. [TEST SUMMARY, lines 2-12]

The two listed failures were:

  1. api/__tests__/billy.name.test.ts - anonymous visitor asking "What's your name?" [TEST SUMMARY JSON, lines 15-20]
  2. api/__tests__/render-decide.test.ts - expected validated report-document PDF bytes rather than a mislabeled fallback. [TEST SUMMARY JSON, lines 22-25]

The archive timestamp is 2026-10-10_01-36-46. This is a snapshot of one run, not a claim about a later test run. [TEST SUMMARY JSON, lines 1-12]

Runtime-map boundary¶

The v3 architecture atlas describes main at commit 03284ea, inspected on 2026-10-08. It is a map of what the repository can demonstrate, not a promise about what is deployed. The atlas does not establish live service availability or a single confirmed production topology. [ATLAS-00, lines 5-12, 31-43; ATLAS-11, lines 5-9, 39-41]

Colophon¶

This is a print companion to the GestaltView Visual Story, not a product audit. It separates the author's stated positions from code-derived architecture notes. Code-derived passages are limited to the v3 repository atlas at 03284ea; configured paths are not represented as proof of live services. The six original principle-card images are reproduced unchanged. Their embedded captions are source wording; surrounding guide copy uses DI terminology. Card 06 retains its original footer overlap. Format: US Letter. Edition: October 2026.
